shouldFix.title: The named join fixtures conflate the CA-1 host spawn decision with its component tail and omit CA-2 from the host-outside-DR-105 case
evidence: FC-JOIN-HOST-OUTSIDE-DR105 says a host-under-instruction CA-1 attempt is not a DR-105 component grant, while FC-JOIN-COMPONENT-TAIL says 'CA-1 spawn ... remain DR-105'. Doctor v4 defines CA-1 itself as spawning an admitted component or running it in-process, so the two class strings overlap on the literal CA-1 SPAWN attempt unless the head/tail boundary is made explicit.

Both recorded host-effect v8 and recorded successor v25 resolve that boundary identically at /coveredActs/CA-1-host-head/subtypes[SPAWN]: 'Decision to spawn an admitted component as a child process. The child's subsequent effects are DR-105.' Thus the spawn decision is the host head governed by the host-effect route; only the spawned component's subsequent effects are the DR-105 tail.

The candidate preserves D-032's two adjacent propositions—that a host-effect contract is necessary before CA-1 host head and that 'component tails (CA-1 spawn, component CA-4 egress)' stay in DR-105—but repeats the shorthand as a fixture without the phase distinction supplied by both recorded host-effect generations. An actor-join candidate must make that seam unambiguous rather than require a future fixture author to infer which occurrence of 'spawn' means the decision and which means the child execution.

FC-JOIN-HOST-OUTSIDE-DR105 enumerates CA-1, CA-3, and CA-4-HOST but omits CA-2, even though D-032 and /extractedDecidedClauses/hostEffectNecessaryNotSufficient enumerate CA-2 alongside all three as a host-effect action outside the component permission vocabulary. CA-2 appears in the unrecorded/fail-closed class, but no named join class tests its actor boundary.

The live artifact applies nothing and its fixture classes are explicitly NAMED-NOT-AUTHORED, so no unsafe execution or false qualification has occurred. That bounds the defect to SHOULD-FIX rather than a blocker.
shouldFix.impact: A future fixture corpus can treat the act of spawning as a DR-105 component grant and thereby skip the host-side authorization head, while never asserting that CA-2 is outside DR-105. That defeats the central head-versus-tail property this integration candidate is meant to carry, even though every surrounding authority disclaimer remains correct.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Make the actor matrix total and phase-exact in the named classes. State that the CA-1 SPAWN decision (and CA-1 IN_PROCESS attempt), CA-2, CA-3, and CA-4-HOST are host-side attempts outside DR-105. State separately that the spawned admitted component's subsequent effects—including component-originated CA-4 egress—remain in DR-105, and explicitly exclude the spawn decision from that tail. Preserve CA-2's independent unexercisable/product prerequisites; this repair clarifies the adopted boundary and does not admit it.
